days.blurb: DriverKit enables hardware driver development as sandboxed user-space processes on macOS, replacing the security-critical practice of loading kernel extensions. DriverKit drivers run in their own restricted process with dedicated entitlements, accessing hardware through a controlled subset of IOKit APIs rather than directly in kernel address space. If a DriverKit driver contains a bug or is exploited, the impact is confined to the driver's user-space process and cannot directly corrupt kernel memory. Apple requires notarization and explicit entitlement approval for DriverKit drivers before enterprise or public distribution, providing a vetting layer for kernel-adjacent code.

SharePlay uses FaceTime's end-to-end encrypted infrastructure to protect the data exchanged during a shared activity, so Apple and other parties outside the activity cannot decrypt it. SharePlay signaling uses the push channel established for FaceTime and activity traffic uses its encrypted data channel. When call membership changes, the key material protecting the activity is re-established: new participants cannot decrypt earlier traffic and removed participants cannot decrypt later traffic. Each activity derives its own key and participant identifiers, isolating apps and reducing cross-activity correlation.

SiriKit integrates third-party apps into Siri using the app extension model, with strict data minimization for user privacy. Before passing personal data to an app's SiriKit extension, Siri checks the app's user-granted permission settings: if the app lacks Contacts access, Siri passes only literal text for relationship references rather than resolved contact data. Custom vocabulary submitted by SiriKit-enabled apps is associated with a random identifier rather than the user's identity, and is purged when the app is deleted or Siri integration is disabled. Only the minimal data needed for the specific user intent is forwarded to the extension process.

Apple laptops implement a hardware-enforced microphone disconnect that physically severs the microphone from the system bus when the lid is closed. This disconnect is implemented at the hardware level and cannot be overridden by software, firmware, or the operating system. The design ensures no application, malware, or compromised kernel can activate the microphone when the device is physically shut. iPad models with detachable keyboards implement equivalent hardware disconnect functionality for the keyboard microphone connector, providing the same physical assurance on those platforms.

Apple's Bluetooth implementation uses Secure Simple Pairing with ECDH P-256 for Classic Bluetooth, generating a link key used to derive AES-CCM session encryption and integrity-protection keys. Bluetooth Low Energy uses LE Secure Connections with P-256 ECDH and AES-CCM-128 for connection encryption. Cross-transport key derivation (CTKD) allows a single pairing ceremony to establish keys for both BR/EDR and BLE transports. BLE devices use randomized advertising addresses rotating periodically to prevent passive tracking. Applications access Bluetooth only through Core Bluetooth, which restricts raw device identifier access and requires user authorization for background operation.

Apple Pay is designed so a device, merchant, and payment network can complete a transaction without exposing a customer's card number to the merchant. The Secure Element stores payment credentials and creates payment-specific cryptograms, while Face ID, Touch ID, Optic ID, or a passcode authorises use when required. Device account numbers, tokenisation, and transaction-specific security values help limit the value of intercepted payment data. Tap to Pay on iPhone extends this model to contactless acceptance using the iPhone's built-in NFC capabilities.

The Apple Account is secured by two-factor authentication using trusted devices and 6-digit time-limited codes. Authentication generates a session token bound to the specific device; account recovery requires knowledge of the account password plus possession of a trusted device or trusted phone number. Managed Apple Accounts, provisioned through Apple School Manager or Apple Business Manager, extend this model to institutional deployments with federated identity provider integration via SAML and SCIM for automated provisioning. Managed accounts are governed by the organization's IdP policies and support supervised enrollment for enterprise and educational device management.

days.blurb: WidgetKit enables app widgets and Apple Watch complications that may display sensitive information in prominent locations including the Lock Screen and Always On display. Developers apply Data Protection entitlements to widget extensions – using NSFileProtectionComplete or NSFileProtectionCompleteUnlessOpen – causing WidgetKit to render placeholder content instead of actual data when the device is locked. Users can independently configure Lock Screen widget visibility in Settings. On Apple Watch, Hide Sensitive Complications globally redacts complication data during Always On mode. Developers must implement the redacted(reason:) callback to supply appropriate placeholder views for privacy-sensitive widget content.
